competitors.name: Brand Finance / Nestlé / Conagra Brands
competitors.action: Grocery Dive reported Brand Finance's estimate that wider GLP-1 adoption puts $73 billion, or roughly one-quarter, of the combined value of the world's 100 most valuable food brands at risk. The article cited frozen-category responses already under way: Nestlé's Vital Pursuit line targets weight-management consumers, while Conagra has added a "GLP-1 friendly" designation to some Healthy Choice frozen meals.

trends.topic: Large food brands adapting portfolios for GLP-1-driven consumption shifts
trends.magnitude: $73 billion of food-brand value identified as exposed; GLP-1 use for weight loss reached 11% of U.S. adults, up from 3% in 2024, according to data cited by Grocery Dive.
trends.context: The $73 billion figure is a brand-valuation scenario rather than a frozen-category sales forecast, and the frozen product examples predate this report. The new risk estimate nevertheless reinforces the competitive direction: frozen brands are using protein, portioning and weight-management cues to defend relevance as households buy fewer calories. Real Dough should expect buyers to ask how premium pizza fits smaller, more intentional eating occasions.

market_data.metric: Food-brand value exposed to GLP-1 adoption
market_data.value: $73 billion across the world's 100 most valuable food brands, roughly one-quarter of their combined $278 billion value
market_data.change: Weight-loss GLP-1 use among U.S. adults reached 11% in September 2026 versus 3% in 2024; households with at least one user spent 6% less on groceries, according to research cited by Grocery Dive

breaking.headline: GLP-1 drugs put $73B in global food value at risk, report finds
